Currently btrfs has a problem where it can use a ridiculous amount of RAM simply
tracking free space.  As free space gets fragmented
column2: we end up with thousands of

column1: entries on an rb-tree per block group
column2: which usually spans 1 gig of area.  Since

column1: we currently don't ever flush free space cache back to disk this gets to be a
bit unweildly on large fs's with lots of fragmentation.
This patch solves this problem by using PAGE_SIZE bitmaps for parts of the free
space cache.  Initially we calculate a threshold of extent entries we can
handle
column2: which is however many extent entries we can cram into 16k of ram.  The

column1: maximum amount of RAM that should ever be used to track 1 gigabyte of diskspace
will be 32k of RAM
column2: which scales much better than we did before.

column1: Once we pass the extent threshold
column2: we start adding bitmaps and using those

column1: instead for tracking the free space.  This patch also makes it so that any free
space thats less than 4 * sectorsize we go ahead and put into a bitmap.  This is
nice since we try and allocate out of the front of a block group
front of a block group is heavily fragmented and then has a huge chunk of free
space at the end
column2: we go ahead and add the fragmented areas to bitmaps and use a

column1: normal extent entry to track the big chunk at the back of the block group.
I've also taken the opportunity to revamp how we search for free space.
Previously we indexed free space via an offset indexed rb tree and a bytes
indexed rb tree.  I've dropped the bytes indexed rb tree and use only the offset
indexed rb tree.  This cuts the number of tree operations we were doing
previously down by half
column2: and gives us a little bit of a better allocation

column1: pattern since we will always start from a specific offset and search forward
from there
column2: instead of searching for the size we need and try and get it as

column1: close as possible to the offset we want.
I've given this a healthy amount of testing pre-new format stuff
post-new format stuff.  I've booted up my fedora box which is installed on btrfs
with this patch and ran with it for a few days without issues.  I've not seen
any performance regressions in any of my tests.
Since the last patch Yan Zheng fixed a problem where we could have overlapping
entries
column2: so updating their offset inline would cause problems.  Thanks
